clue.text: Fresh title adopted by infernal poet and dabbler

indicators.note: something adopted is taken in, so the reworked letters go inside the poet's name

parts.note: Dante Alighieri, the poet of the Inferno, hence infernal

indicators.note: a fresh version is a new one, so the letters of the word title are rearranged

explanation.surface: A newly conferred title is taken up by a hellish poet and an amateur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fresh' signals the anagram of TITLE and 'adopted by' the insertion into the poet's name. 'Infernal' is a nod to Dante's Inferno, not a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who dabbles in an art without real commitment is a superficial amateur, the meaning of the Italian-derived word.

clue.text: Money offering a right to support party lines?

indicators.note: in a down answer a piece that supports another sits below it

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration
LL is the abbreviation for lines, a plural of L

explanation.surface: Cash given so that a right-wing stance props up the party's official policy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party lines' looks like one political phrase but splits into two separate pieces; 'to support' means sitting below in a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The dollar is the currency unit of the United States and many other countries, so it stands for money.

clue.text: Left one opening to tie up

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
a gate is an opening in a fence or wall

explanation.surface: Someone left a gap and must now fasten things together.
explanation.definitionFit: To ligate is the surgical verb for binding a vessel with a thread, so it means to tie up.

clue.text: Such votes unusually hit new helpers welcoming Independent

indicators.note: to welcome is to take someone in, so the single letter goes inside the scrambled letters
doing something unusually means in a different way, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the abbreviation for Independent, as on a ballot paper

explanation.surface: Parliamentary votes are strangely affected by new aides who welcome an independent member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusually' rearranges HIT NEW HELPERS and 'welcoming' takes in I. In the UK Parliament a three-line whip is the strictest instruction from party managers to attend and vote.
explanation.definitionFit: Party managers mark the most important divisions with a triple underline, meaning members must turn up and vote as told.

clue.text: A variable list on poems down under

parts.note: in algebra n is a standard symbol for a variable quantity
to list is to lean over, as does tip
odes are lyric poems

explanation.surface: A changing list on poems describing the lower half of a page.
explanation.walkthrough: 'List' is the nautical sense, to lean, not a catalogue.
explanation.definitionFit: Australia and New Zealand, opposite Britain on the globe, are called the Antipodes, and colloquially down under.

clue.text: Rubbish remains after tower evacuated

indicators.note: after puts the remains below the tower's shell in this down answer
an evacuated building is emptied, so only the outer letters of tower are kept

parts.note: ash is what remains after burning, as in cremated remains

explanation.surface: Debris left once a tower has been cleared of people.
explanation.definitionFit: Trash is the American word for refuse or garbage, a direct synonym for rubbish.

clue.text: Friends from the east? Precisely

indicators.note: in an across answer reading from the east means right to left, so the word is backwards

parts.note: pals are friends

explanation.surface: Are these companions coming exactly from the eastern side?
explanation.definitionFit: As an adverb, as in slap in the middle, the word means exactly or directly.

clue.text: Hang on desperately in case of lad writing

indicators.note: in places the scrambled letters within the outer letters of lad
a case is the outside, so the first and last letters of lad are used
acting desperately means wildly, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A boy clings on frantically, in the case of the lad's handwriting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desperately' rearranges HANG ON to ONGHAN, and 'in' puts that between L and D, the 'case of lad'.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing done by hand with a pen, rather than typed or in shorthand, is called by this name.

clue.text: Mate should keep a short chronicle of vicar's work

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it within, so the letters go inside the friend's word

parts.note: a mate is a pal

indicators.note: short means cut off, so the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a chronicle is a story or account

explanation.surface: A friend ought to preserve a brief record of the vicar's activities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' drops the last letter of the chronicle word, and 'should keep' puts that and A inside the friend.
explanation.definitionFit: A clergyman's care of the parish flock is called pastoral work, from the image of a shepherd tending sheep.

clue.text: Jump on Conservative, inclined to get seasonal work at home

parts.note: to spring is to jump
leaning means inclined or tilted

explanation.surface: Jumping on the Tories, keen to tackle a seasonal job around the house.
explanation.definitionFit: A thorough domestic clean-up traditionally done once winter ends is named after the season it happens in.

clue.text: Trail behind Her Majesty getting a drink

indicators.note: behind means the queen's letters follow the trailing word

parts.note: to trail is to lag behind
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen

explanation.surface: Following the Queen around while being handed something to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is the royal cipher of Elizabeth Regina.
explanation.definitionFit: A lager is a light, fizzy beer, the commonest drink ordered in a British pub.

clue.text: Beefy sending son to back for accoutrements

indicators.note: sending something means moving it elsewhere in the word
to the back means to the end of the word

parts.note: a beefy person is strapping, big and strong

explanation.surface: A burly man packs his son off to the rear to fetch the gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sending' and 'to back' move the S of STRAPPING from the front to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Accoutrements are the outward equipment and accessories of a role, the ornamental extras that go with it.

clue.text: A fool to be attached to northern city

parts.note: a twerp is a silly person, a fool

explanation.surface: An idiot destined to be tied to a city in the north.
explanation.definitionFit: Antwerp is a major port city in Flanders, in northern Belgium.

clue.text: Expression of weariness coming from house on hill, mostly

indicators.note: in an across answer on means coming after the hill letters
mostly means not quite all, so the last letter of the word is cut

parts.note: a height is a hill or high ground

explanation.surface: A tired sigh issuing from a house on a hilltop.
explanation.definitionFit: This old interjection, familiar from the dwarfs' song, voices boredom, tiredness or resignation.

clue.text: Taking collagen daily may reveal an ulterior motive!

parts.note: these two words conceal, across their boundary, the six letters of a word for a list of business, exactly as the answer read as an instruction says

explanation.surface: A beauty supplement routine may betray some secret purpose!
explanation.walkthrough: The answer read as an instruction describes the clue itself: the six letters spanning the end of collagen and the start of daily are concealed there.
explanation.definitionFit: A secret aim kept behind a plausible public reason is a concealed plan, an ulterior motive.

clue.text: Apple is beyond compare

definitions.meaning: an old variety of dessert apple carries this name
without equal, unrivalled, from the French for having no equal

explanation.surface: An apple that has no rival.
explanation.definitionFit: The French-derived word means peerless, and it is also the name of a historic English dessert apple variety.

clue.text: Given accommodation and invoiced to include rent regularly

indicators.note: to include something is to hold it within, so the letters go inside

parts.note: to be invoiced is to be billed

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter, here the second and fourth of rent

explanation.surface: Housed somewhere and sent a bill that takes in the rent each month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' takes E and T from rEnT; 'to include' puts them inside BILLED.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers are billeted when they are lodged in private houses, so the word means housed or quartered.

clue.text: Number employed by European comedian likely to bring in a profit

definitions.text: likely to bring in a profit

indicators.note: being employed by a firm means being taken in, so the number goes within

parts.note: a comic is a comedian

explanation.surface: A routine performed by a continental comic which ought to make money.
explanation.definitionFit: An economic rent or venture is one that pays its way, yielding enough return to be profitable.

clue.text: More and more home care must be arranged individually

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: things that are arranged are put in order, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: singly means one at a time, individually

explanation.surface: Domestic care must be organised person by person, ever more so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Must be arranged' is the anagram signal on care; 'home' is the familiar crossword sense of being in.
explanation.definitionFit: An adverb describing something growing steadily, to an ever greater degree.

clue.text: National may be like this country in Africa

parts.note: so means in this way, like this
Mali is a country in West Africa

explanation.surface: A citizen could resemble an African state.
explanation.definitionFit: A national is a citizen of a nation; this word names a citizen of the Horn of Africa state.

clue.text: My new job includes year five English

indicators.note: including something means holding it inside, so the year letter goes into the reworked letters
a new form of the word is a fresh arrangement of its letters

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral five

explanation.surface: A fresh post that takes in Year Five English teaching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges JOB to BJO and 'includes' puts Y after the B. 'My' is the exclamation of surprise, not the possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are dated exclamations of surprise, used in the same breath as gosh or goodness.

clue.text: Institutes needing no area for meals

indicators.note: needing no means doing without, so the letter is taken out

parts.note: to institute something is to launch it

explanation.surface: Bodies that require no premises for their dinners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Institutes' looks like a noun, organisations, but is the verb, to set up.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural of the midday meal, so it fits the plural noun meals as examples of them.

clue.text: Got a whiff of fish

definitions.meaning: detected an odour, the past tense of the verb for sensing by nose
a small silvery food fish of the salmon family

explanation.definitionFit: The past tense of the verb for perceiving an odour, which is also the name of a small edible sea fish.

clue.text: Particle absorbed by some or other science

indicators.note: something absorbed is taken in, so the particle goes inside

parts.note: any means some or other, unspecified
an atom is a tiny particle

explanation.surface: A particle taken up by some science or another.
explanation.definitionFit: The study of the structure of the body is a branch of biological science.

clue.text: What might measure article on the fourth dimension?

indicators.note: in an across answer on means the article word follows the dimension word

parts.note: time is often called the fourth dimension after length, breadth and height
a piece is an article, as in a newspaper

explanation.surface: A query about what could gauge a journal paper on the fourth dimension.
explanation.definitionFit: A clock or watch is an instrument that may measure the passing hours.

clue.text: Form of insect giving single male a turn

parts.note: I, the Roman numeral one, means single
a go is a turn, as in a game

explanation.surface: A bug's shape gives a lone man his chance.
explanation.definitionFit: The final, adult stage of an insect's metamorphosis, as a winged butterfly after the pupa.

clue.text: Reportedly pushed under water pipe

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so a word is said and its sound kept

parts.note: to duck someone is to push them under water

explanation.surface: Word is that someone was shoved under the water by a pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: A tube or channel carrying fluid or cables, such as a tear channel or air shaft.

clue.text: A good child on endless trail that's seen in cave

indicators.note: in an across answer on means these pieces come after the shortened word
endless means without its end, so the last letter is cut off

parts.note: to stalk is to trail or follow stealthily
a mite is a small child

explanation.surface: A well-behaved youngster on an unending trek through caves.
explanation.definitionFit: A column of mineral built up from a cave floor by dripping water, the counterpart of one hanging from the roof.
